key_insight: Robo-Saber is the first system that automatically generates VR headset and controller motions from in-game object arrangements, using style exemplars and score-alignment to produce skilled, diverse virtual players for playtesting.
problem_solved: Automates realistic, scalable VR playtesting by producing diverse player motions (headset + controllers) that reflect different play styles and skill levels—addressing the lack of tools to simulate credible VR user behavior for game evaluation.
method: Train a conditional motion generator on the large BOXRR-23 dataset to map in-game object arrangements to headset and controller trajectories.
Condition generation on style exemplars to capture varied player behaviors and skill signatures.
Align or optimize generated motions to maximize simulated gameplay score, and validate the model on Beat Saber to produce skilled, diverse virtual players.
impact: Enables automated, repeatable VR playtesting and rapid design iteration, reducing reliance on human testers and providing a benchmarkable way to evaluate level difficulty and player experience. It also advances motion synthesis and simulated human behavior modeling in ML.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: level/object-arrangement → style exemplar + generator → simulated headset & controller trajectories → scoring/evaluation
Side-by-side overlay: real player motion vs. Robo-Saber-generated motion (controller and head paths)
Score vs. style scatter/heatmap: distribution of simulated gameplay scores across different style exemplars and skill levels
Trajectory timeline: example time-series of controller orientation/position and headset movement during a Beat Saber sequence
paper_title: Robo-Saber: Generating and Simulating Virtual Reality Players
paper_authors: Nam Hee Kim, Jingjing May Liu, Jaakko Lehtinen, Perttu Hämäläinen, James F. O'Brien
